first_impression.reaction: My assistant sent this over while we were shortlisting who could handle the honeymoon after the wedding. The first screen is calm and it doesn't shout a 'from' price, which is a relief. But it reads like advice for a couple watching every dollar: chargebacks, AUSTRAC, exchange margins. Nothing tells me this team has done a trip at our level or how they treat privacy. My assistant would summarise it as 'sensible, generic, nothing about discretion' and I'd read the section on how they work and the closing, nothing more.

journey.quote: A number on its own tells you very little.
journey.reaction: Agreed. I don't want a number, I want to know what's possible. A good, quiet opening.

journey.section: What you are paying a planner for
journey.quote: the late check-out, the dietary note, the quiet table on the last night.
journey.reaction: These are nice touches, but they're small. For us the details are closing a villa to other guests, a private terminal, our own security working with the hotel's. The scale feels modest.

journey.section: What you are paying a planner for
journey.quote: If you would rather start from a ready shape and tailor it, browse our [honeymoon packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-honeymoon-packages).
journey.reaction: Packages. This is exactly the moment I start wondering if I'd be treated like a standard client.

journey.section: What moves the cost of the trip
journey.quote: **Private or shared.** A private boat, guide or dinner is a different booking from a shared tour or a set menu.
journey.reaction: The only line that speaks to how we travel. Shared tours and set menus aren't on our list at all.

journey.section: How planners may charge, as questions to ask
journey.quote: A good planner answers each of these without hesitation.
journey.reaction: Fine. My family office would ask these anyway. It doesn't need to be explained to me.

journey.section: Paying in Australian dollars or another currency
journey.quote: Money transfer services in Australia must be registered with AUSTRAC, so check that before you use one.
journey.reaction: This is far too much explaining for me. Our office handles payments. A whole section on exchange margins tells me who the page is really written for.

journey.quote: Some banks allow a chargeback, reversing a disputed card transaction, if you do not receive what you paid for
journey.reaction: Useful for someone, not for me. It makes the brand feel like it's preparing for things going wrong.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor looks after you from start to finish, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: Good. One person who knows us is what we want. Fewer people means fewer leaks.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: Nothing is too early or too vague.
journey.reaction: A bit eager, but harmless. I'd rather hear that they can handle anything than that they'll accept anything.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in Australian dollars.
journey.reaction: We live in Dubai and in London. Australian dollars is fine for comparison, but it tells me they think of their client as Australian, not international.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Concierge honeymoon fee charged: flat, percentage, commission or a mix? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland receive commissions from the hotels and suppliers it books? (deferred business detail)
Have you planned honeymoons with exclusive-use villas, private aviation or a security detail, and can you show me one, discreetly? (deferred business detail)
What perks or access come with booking through you, such as Wedded Privileges? (deferred business detail)
What is the typical range for a fully managed private honeymoon? (deferred business detail)
How do you handle confidentiality: NDAs, guest names, nothing on social media?
Can I deal with you through my assistant or family office, and can the quote be in another currency if we ask?

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would rather start from a ready shape and tailor it, browse our [honeymoon packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-honeymoon-packages).
turn_offs_found.why: Package language is the quickest way to make me feel like a standard client. It sits early, in the section about what I'm paying for.

turn_offs_found.quote: Money transfer services in Australia must be registered with AUSTRAC, so check that before you use one.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. Together with the exchange-margin and chargeback paragraphs, it makes the page read like budget protection advice, not a premium planner talking.

would_share_with: Nobody. My assistant would file it as 'sensible but generic' and not forward it.

cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a public form off a blog post. I'd need a referral or a private introduction, and something on the page that shows they've done this at our scale and keep it quiet. The single Advisor and fee in writing are good, but nothing here says discretion.

top_3_changes: Move or drop the packages link in 'What you are paying a planner for' ('If you would rather start from a ready shape and tailor it, browse our honeymoon packages.') so package language doesn't appear in the section about what the fee buys.

Tighten the currency and protection sections (AUSTRAC, exchange margins, chargebacks) into a short checklist so the page doesn't over-explain; the advice stays, it just stops dominating the second half.

Add generic trip levers for the top end to 'What moves the cost of the trip', such as exclusive use, private transfers and privacy or security arrangements, framed as reader advice to ask any planner about, not as a claim about Wedded Wonderland.
